findings.claim: Builder summary: MC is a new 'exact' check that 'detects every case FA detects' (frozen claim_to_be_tested: every undeclared dependency that changes row bits is detected unless rounding-limited).
findings.evidence: /home/cosmosapjw/.cargo-targets/vigilode-loop-20261116/w3-v26/review-scratch/probe/src/main.rs (cancel), logs/probe_cancel.log: declared tridiagonal n=60 (construction B, moduli 3,4,5), row 30 also reads (y0-y45)+(y1-y16) with equal values: FA@seq, FA_P@t2, FA_P@t6 -> UndeclaredEntry{row 30, column 0}; build, S8, MC@seq, MC@t6, MC_P@t3, MC_P@t6 pass. True ring n=84 (construction G, primes 2,3,5), row 40 reads (y0-y30)+(y3-y63): same. Row bits differ with/without each omitted column at all 4 MC states (not rounding-limited by the frozen rule); couplings have coefficient 1. Unpaired control (0,44,1,17): MC detects. Generic rows with 2-3 omissions (logs/probe_multi.log, 6376 cases): no one-sided result, so the blind spot needs pairwise cancellation under every colouring.
findings.correction: Scope 'exact' and 'detects every case FA detects' to the frozen corpus (one undeclared dependency per row, all wrong cases under construction B). State in REPORT/RESULTS that the general claim is refuted: a row whose several undeclared couplings cancel pairwise at the checked state under every colouring passes MC (and S8) but not FA. This matters for the owner's default decision.
